notes: Source identity independently established from the supplied canonical text: title Oral Approach–Avoidance: Affective Consequences of Muscular Articulation Dynamics; authors Sascha Topolinski, Ira Theresa Maschmann, Diane Pecher, and Piotr Winkielman; Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2014, 106(6), 885–896; DOI 10.1037/a0036477. The candidate contains the full primary research article through p. 896, rather than an abstract or secondary account. No PDF was supplied. Both assigned rows explicitly identify original Study 2 and p. 888, regardless of their distinct replication experiment labels. Table 1 identifies Experiment 2 by German psychology undergraduates, Pool A, and names of gourmet food companies. The Results section on p. 889 explicitly links Table 1 to the single comparisons between inward versus outward words using averaged preference ratings. Thus its printed N is the participant sample for the target comparison, not the pooled six-experiment count or the a priori power requirement. N is directly printed; no arithmetic or derivation from degrees of freedom was used. Participant exclusions for Experiment 2 are not specified. Only n_o was assigned; all other side/field values are unassigned placeholders.
